_comment: This file is read by the app as www-data AND by /usr/local/bin/cars-nginx-render as root.
The registry password has to be readable by both, so 640 root:www-data - not 600.
Everything except registry.pass can be changed later and takes effect on the next action.
_shared_api: true when api_dir is ONE copy shared by every client, which is this server's
arrangement: the same build and the same api/ serve /<folder>/ for all of them.
Leave it unset to let the server work it out from the filesystem (api_dir's
parent has no index.html). Set it explicitly when it matters, because a wrong
answer is quiet: each client gets a private api/ copy, and the next deploy
_api_dir: Where the shared api/ lives. Its PARENT is the deployment root: /var/www.
_webroot: The deployment root the rendered server block serves out of. The
renderer refuses to write a server block without it, and it is not
derivable from api_dir alone: api/ can sit beside the tenants (/var/www/api)
or inside one (/var/www/acme/api), and those need different roots.
_canonical_build: The one build every client's folder is copied from, on every deploy.
It must NOT be inside /var/www/api and must NOT be a tenant folder.
Keep it out of the nginx web root if you can: nothing should be able to fetch it.
_template_database: The reference-only database every new client is built from.
It must have the schema and the reference rows (brands, roles, permissions,
the admin account) and NONE of the client data - 38 business tables that are
empty in a fresh build. Provisioning refuses a template that has any, so a
template built from a live tenant fails loudly instead of shipping one
client's dropdown options to the next.
Leave it unset only if you intend to pass seed_source per run.
_web_group: Group given write access to a new tenant's folders. Empty means do not chgrp.
_php_socket: ls /run/php/php*-fpm.sock - pick the one nginx actually fastcgi_pass's to.
This has to match the existing vhosts or only this file will work.
_server_name: The IP clients reach this on. One vhost serves every client by URL prefix.
_cert_dir: Let's Encrypt live/ directory for server_name. The renderer refuses to write a
server block without it rather than emitting a path that does not exist.
For a bare IP this needs certbot >= 5.4 (short-lived IP certificates):
_default_server: true makes this the catch-all for its address and port. Required for a bare IP,
because a browser sends no SNI for an address, so the block cannot be matched by
name. If another vhost already holds that position, nginx -t fails with
"duplicate default server" - the render is rolled back and nothing changes.
Then either drop default_server from the other block or set this to false.
Mutually exclusive with ip_address: that vhost takes the slot instead.
_ip_address: Set only when the server is reached BOTH by a domain and by a bare IP and the
same app must answer on both. Adds a second :443 vhost - same body, its own
server_name, own certificate, and the default_server slot (no SNI arrives for
an address) - so default_server must be false when this is set.
The certificate has to be a separate, short-lived (6-day) Let's Encrypt IP
certificate, because the classic profile carries DNS names only:
Needs certbot >= 5.4; renewals run from the normal certbot.timer.
Leave empty on a single-name server: server_name/cert_dir already describe it.
_ip_cert_dir: Where certbot put the IP certificate. Defaults to /etc/letsencrypt/live/<ip_address>; set only if certbot named it differently.
_ipv6: false omits the [::] listen lines. A kernel without IPv6 makes [::] a fatal bind
error, which would stop nginx starting for every site on the machine.
_render_command: The root-owned script the Provision screen runs through sudo. It is what the
sudoers rule names, and it must be the path in the sudoers file exactly.
_render_php: The PHP that produces the config text, read by cars-nginx-render as root.
It lives OUTSIDE the web root on purpose. Root executes it, so if the web
server's user could write it, a file-write bug in the app would be a root
cars-nginx-render refuses to run it if it is not root-owned, or if it is
_render_output: Where the rendered config is installed. Must be under /etc/nginx.
That symlink is the one-time step; nothing afterwards has to be done by hand.

_comment: Credentials for the dbs table that lists the clients.
Needed here because the renderer runs under sudo, where the environment that
api/config.php reads from has been scrubbed - it cannot fall back to that.
